planting.note: Plant container-grown or rooted-cutting trees in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Ice Crystal is grown as much for its oddly puckered, deeply lobed leaves as for its fruit, and it has earned the UK Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit on the strength of that foliage display.

directions: Ice Crystal stands out among common-type figs for its crinkled, heavily textured foliage, which gives the whole plant an unusual, almost frosted appearance even before any fruit forms. It is grown as widely for this ornamental foliage effect in cool-summer climates like the UK as it is for its fruit, which is a modest, secondary bonus rather than the main draw. Like other common-type figs it is self-fertile and needs no caprification, so a single plant in well-drained soil and full sun will crop on its own. Give it the same winter protection as other half-hardy figs in borderline climates, since it is grown more for its leaves than bred for extreme cold tolerance.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container trees in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; Zidi is a Smyrna-type fig from traditional Moroccan orchards and, like Calimyrna, will not set its main crop without caprification by the fig wasp from a nearby caprifig.

directions: Zidi is one of the traditional Smyrna-type fig cultivars long grown in Moroccan fig orchards, prized for fruit that dries well and has sustained local fresh and dried-fig production for generations. As a true Smyrna type it depends on caprification, meaning its flowers must receive pollen carried by the fig wasp Blastophaga psenes from an inedible caprifig growing nearby, or the main crop drops before ripening. This makes it impractical in humid regions lacking the wasp, and best suited to hot, dry-summer climates similar to its native growing areas. Provide the same deep, well-drained soil and minimal winter pruning as other figs, with steady irrigation while fruit sizes up to reduce splitting.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container trees in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; Marabout is a Smyrna-type North African fig that, like Calimyrna and Zidi, needs caprification from a nearby caprifig to set its main crop.

directions: Marabout belongs to the Smyrna group of fig cultivars traditionally grown across North African fig-producing regions, where its fruit has long been valued for drying alongside other local Smyrna-type figs. Because it is a true Smyrna type, it will not finish its main crop without caprification: pollen carried by the fig wasp Blastophaga psenes from a nearby inedible caprifig must reach the flowers inside the fruit, or the developing figs drop unripe. This dependency limits reliable fruiting to hot, arid growing regions where the wasp's breeding cycle overlaps with bloom, making it a poor fit for humid climates. Grow it in deep, well-drained soil in full sun with the same light winter pruning used for other fig types, and irrigate evenly as fruit matures to limit splitting.
